assign.tab: Claude Code - monorepo - Visual Studio Code
assign.request: See what minions are able to test, from a UI/UX standpoint, by driving the browser (mcp or playwright or both). Write a report about what MCP can do via eval, what it can't do, what Chrome Dev Protocol could do, what Playwright can do, what each can't do, etc. Extend mcp-tab-awareness/comparison.md into report.md answering what each driver can TEST on ext/Panel.
steps: block dev socket, launch headless Playwright
try grip drag gesture (eval, Playwright, CDP)
try display-word toolbar gesture (eval, Playwright, CDP)

log.msg: Playwright real input: all 3 gestures work on the no-saver demo panels (workspace() top left untouched, socket blocked defense-in-depth) — split ghost+commit, grip drag (+100px matched the pointer move), display->grid overlay drew 2 tracks. 6 pngs saved.

CDP: Input.dispatchMouseEvent mouseMoved genuinely sets :hover (pointer-events auto on .panel-edge) — a real gate a JS eval dispatch cannot trigger; raw click opened the split ghost, second click sequencing needs tuning (partial commit). Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride resized window.innerWidth 1400->480 with zero Playwright setViewportSize call — confirmed viewport-without-window-resize. CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode returned 5 rules w/ origin (user-agent, regular) for .panel-grip natively, no getComputedStyle reconstruction needed. 3 pngs.

site eval, on my own socket-connected tab (no-saver demo panels only): dispatchEvent bypasses hit-testing entirely — edge stayed pointer-events:none (no real :hover) but a direct click dispatch on it still fired split.js and committed. Grip drag needed the event on the grip element itself (not document) plus an awaited double-rAF before coalesce()s queued resize applied (delta 0 -> 100 once awaited) — a real timing trap unique to eval. Display->grid also worked once targeted correctly (8 overlay children). Net: eval CAN drive all 3 gestures, but tests the HANDLER not real reachability, and needs app-internals knowledge (exact listener target, rAF timing) that Playwright/CDP real input never needs. Hidden-tab visibilityState did not toggle for a 2nd headless page brought to front in the same context (a Playwright headless quirk, not counter-evidence against the known hidden-tab verdict already on record).

assign.outcome: **Playwright is the workhorse for Panel gestures; `eval` is wasted effort for driving them.** Tried split/drag/display-change with site `eval`, Playwright, and CDP on ext/Panel's no-saver demo panels (persisted workspace() untouched; dev socket blocked for Playwright/CDP). All 3 drove all 3 gestures, but `eval` only by dispatching straight at the listener-owning element (bypassing real hit-testing/`:hover`) and hand-timing the app's rAF — reverse-engineering the code, not testing it. Playwright gave real hit-tested input for free. CDP's unique wins: `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` (viewport resize, no window resize — verified 1400→480), `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` (matched rules + origin, natively), and `mouseMoved` setting genuine `:hover`. Report: [report.md](./report.md) (39 lines). Evidence: 9 pngs in this dir. Left undone: `CSS.forcePseudoState`, and a from-scratch hidden-tab reproduction (Playwright headless multi-page didn't toggle `visibilityState` — a tool quirk, not new evidence against the standing hidden-tab verdict).
